claims.assertion: The trip is a RydeTAXI metered ride (total charged $46.18 with distance $31.30 for 22.20 km and time $9.38), so extra kilometres driven translate directly into a higher fare; the rider paid more than the optimal-route distance supports.

The GPS record shows one off-route segment (10:13–10:24) in which 7.21 km were driven where the optimal route covers 2.29 km, adding 4.92 km and straying up to 1794 m from the optimal route; that segment is unexempted unless the driver proves an exemption.
Per RD-2, the refund on that unexempted segment is its added distance times this trip's per-km rate: 4.92 km × $1.4099/km = $6.94 (SGD), rounded to the cent.

The rider's only message before the segment was 'Sure, your call.' in reply to the driver's 'mind if I go round via Clementi Avenue 2?'; 'your call' hands the route to the driver and is at most a general route choice, not an agreement to any specific road, and the record contains no stop, location message or road-name fact placing the car on Clementi Avenue 2.

The driver's claim of a breakdown reroute (a written statement made after the trip, not chat) does not match the traffic record for the segment: the only incident (vehicle breakdown, 09:47, 0 m from the optimal route) sits on the Ayer Rajah Expressway, while the off-route segment started at 10:13, after the AYE band-2 congestion window ended at 10:13.

Under RD-4(a), an incident only exempts a segment when it is on the optimal route and its reported_at falls before that segment began and remains listed in the trip window; the AYE breakdown is at 0 m from the optimal route but the detour runs 10:13–10:24, so at most the AYE portion ahead of 10:13 could be covered, not the full 4.92 km added at 10:13–10:24.

A speed band alone cannot exempt the segment: RD-4(b) makes band 1–2 records corroboration only, and in any event the only such record (AYE band 2) expired at 10:13 when the detour began, while the alternative roads recorded (Clementi/Jurong Town Hall corridor band 5, CTE band 4) show no severe congestion.

The waiting fee billed was only $0.13 for 0.5 min and no other unpublished add-on appears in the breakdown (base $3.90 + distance $31.30 + time $9.38 + waiting $0.13 + platform $1.47), so the rider's claim is confined to the detour mileage, not to a fare-schedule breach.
Neither party has an upheld dispute in the last 90 days (rider 0/1, driver 0/1), so RD-6's repeated-violation threshold is not met and no account flag is sought on this record.

weaknesses: The rider's 'Sure, your call.' (F9) answers a driver message naming a road (F8); the other side will argue this is at least a general route authorisation under RD-5, and if the judge reads 'your call' as leaving the route entirely to the driver, the whole 4.92 km added could be treated as consented rather than only the Clementi Avenue 2 portion being undetermined.

Traffic facts cut against us in part: a vehicle breakdown is recorded at 0 m from the optimal route (F15) and the AYE was at band 2 until 10:13 (F12), so the driver will argue RD-4(a) immunity for the AYE stretch (F3 segment starts 10:13), which could reduce or eliminate the exempted distance and therefore our $6.94 figure.
